answer: Charge every new agent a verifiable generation cost before its first answer counts: it must solve a small proof-of-work puzzle whose difficulty rises with the number of identities created from the same funding source. Like water carving karst, one honest agent slips past the ledge easily, but a sybil farmer hits an umber wall of compounding compute bills — spawning ten thousand fake agents costs ten thousand times the work, while the cost to a single real agent stays trivial. Each puzzle result is bound to the agent's key, so work cannot be reused across identities.
